title: A collective's perceptual field and ability to find alternative paths grow with its size

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A collective's perceptual field and ability to find alternative paths grow with its size

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Extending William James' definition of intelligence (reaching the same goal by different means) to collectives via the perceptual field, the region of space and time an agent can survey for alternative paths to a goal, the authors propose that as a collective grows its perceptual field increases, improving its ability to find variant paths.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As the size of a collective increases its perceptual field increases, improving its ability to find variant paths.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction”. Scope: Cell collectives and other biological collectives

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Route diversity and sensing range can be operationalized, and existing swarm and cell-collective studies provide partial tests. The universal monotonic proposal across biological collectives lacks harmonized coverage.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define perceptual field as the spatiotemporal range influencing decisions and measure alternative-route success against collective size across controlled obstacle tasks.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Perceptual field has multiple possible measures.

Collective size covaries with density, sensing, and available force.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement extends a definition of intelligence and then proposes that larger collectives survey more and therefore find more paths. Under that definition the first step does not come apart from 'more cells can sense more'. No observation is specified that would distinguish the proposal from that tautology.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: If the perceptual field is defined as the region of space and time a collective can survey, adding members enlarges that region by the definition used in the statement. No task, path metric or rival is given that would let 'improved search for variant paths' fail while the collective was still larger.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No dataset of cell collectives pairs group size with a count of alternative paths actually found.

Growth of a survey region with the number of sensors is stipulated rather than measured.

fields.label: Dimension scores

operationalizability: 0.28
